title: Box 2.01 Risk factors for oesophageal adenocarcinoma (OAC)
tablehtml:
Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD)

·    GORD is the single most important risk factor, although the relationship is complex as only a subset of patients with GORD develop Barrett oesophagus and are at risk of OAC

·    The risk of OAC in patients with Barret oesophagus is 10–55 times the risk in the general population {29671158}

·    Individuals with reflux disease without oesophageal erosion do not seem to be at increased risk for OAC {37704252}

Obesity

·    Abdominal obesity is strongly associated with an increased risk of GORD {29671158}

·    Obesity might also increase the risk of Barrett oesophagus and OAC independent of GORD; this may be related to proinflammatory cytokines (e.g. insulin-like growth factors) {29671158}

Male sex

·    OAC and Barrett oesophagus are characterized by a strong male predominance, with an M:F ratio in OAC incidence as high as 6:1 {32918910}

·    Estrogen might protect against (and androgen might promote) the development of OAC {29037468;29342161}

·    Sex-specific genetic variants associate with gastro-oesophageal reflux and OAC risk in male individuals {32918910}

Smoking

·    Smoking increases the risk of Barrett oesophagus and OAC, although the association is less strong compared with other risk factors {29671158;29037468}

Helicobacter pylori infection

·    H. pylori infection is inversely associated with the risk of OAC {29671158;29037468}; a possible mechanism is reduced volume and acidity of gastric juice in atrophic gastritis after longstanding infection

Antireflux therapies

·    GORD symptom control and reflux oesophagitis healing are clear indications for antireflux therapies; studies support a chemopreventive effect with regard to Barrett oesophagus progression to OAC {30057104}

·    Patients with Barrett oesophagus who undergo antireflux surgery do not have a lower risk of OAC than those using antireflux medication {37690771}

Medications

·    NSAIDs (including acetylsalicylic acid) and statins have shown inverse associations with the development of OAC {29671158;29037468}, but large controlled clinical trials are needed to confirm the protective effect of these drugs

Dietary factors

·    The consumption of dietary fibre, vegetables, vitamins, minerals, meat (in particular red meat), and fats has been associated with different risks of reflux oesophagitis, Barrett oesophagus, and OAC; however, these associations require confirmation in larger population studies {29037468}

title: Table 2.02 The Mandard, Becker, College of American Pathologists (CAP) / modified Ryan, and Japan Esophageal Society (JES) systems for assessing the tumour regression grade (TRG) of carcinoma after neoadjuvant therapy {8194005;28918544;31664618;38512393}
tablehtml:
Mandard

Becker

CAP / modified Ryan

Japan Esophageal Society

TRG 1: Absence of residual cancer with fibrosis extending throughout (complete response)

TRG 1a: No carcinoma present

Score 0: Complete response

No viable cancer cells

Grade 3: Markedly effective

No viable cancer cells are evident

TRG 2: Rare residual cancer cells scattered through the fibrosis

TRG 1b: < 10% residual carcinoma present

Score 1: Near-complete response

Single cells or rare small groups of cancer cells

Grade 2: Moderately effective

Viable cancer cells account for less than one third of the tumour area, whereas other cancer cells are severely degenerated or necrotic

TRG 3: An increase in the number of residual cancer cells, but fibrosis still predominates

TRG 2: 10–50% residual carcinoma present

Score 2: Partial response

Residual cancer with evident tumour regression, but more than single cells or rare small groups of cancer cells

TRG 4: Residual cancer outgrowing fibrosis

TRG 3: > 50% residual carcinoma present

Score 3: Poor or no response

Extensive residual cancer with no evident tumour regression

Grade 1: Slightly effective

Viable cancer cells (including those with eosinophilic cytoplasm with vacuolation and swollen nuclei) account for one third or more of the tumour tissue; however, there is some evidence of degeneration of cancer tissue or cellsa

TRG 5: Absence of regressive changes

Grade 0: Ineffective

No recognizable cytological or histological therapeutic effect

aJES grade 1 is subdivided into grade 1a (viable cancer cells account for at least two thirds of the tumour area) and grade 1b (viable cancer cells account for at least one third but less than two thirds of the tumour area).

legend: In addition to an adenocarcinoma, this image also features a leiomyoma and a zone of reactive squamous hyperplasia(pseudoepitheliiomatous hyperplasia)
Oesophageal adenocarcinoma presenting as an ulcerative growth; note the mucosal changes adjacent to the adenocarcinoma, constituting dysplasia and Barrett oesophagus.
An example detected by endoscopy.
Papillary pattern.
C Oesophageal adenocarcinoma with signet-ring cell pattern.
A Immunohistochemistry indicates an ERBB2 (HER2) immunoscore of 3+ for this tumour; note the lateral membrane and basolateral membrane staining.
C An adenocarcinoma treated with preoperative chemoradiation, showing clear cell change in the tumour and calcification and foamy macrophages in the stroma.
Tubular pattern.
Oesophageal adenocarcinoma in Barrett oesophagus with a double layer of muscularis mucosae.
Mucinous pattern.

B Silver-enhanced in situ hybridization confirms the presence of ERBB2 (HER2) amplification; the black dots represent amplified ERBB2 signals and the red dots represent diploid CEP17 signals. FISH can also be used to confirm ERBB2 amplification, but many authorities recommend silver-enhanced in situ hybridization over FISH for testing upper GI tract adenocarcinomas.
Macroscopic appearance after neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

diagnosis: Molecular underpinnings of the development of oesophageal adenocarcinoma
legend: Progression to adenocarcinoma from non-dysplastic Barrett oesophagus is driven by a synergistic cascade of TP53 mutations, epigenetic modifications, and increasing chromosomal structural alterations and copy-number variations.

diagnosis: Oesophageal adenocarcinoma after neoadjuvant systemic treatment
legend: A Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) specimen with an early (pT1a) oesophageal adenocarcinoma extending to lateral mucosal margins of excision (arrows). This should not be confused with a positive deep margin. True submucosa is highlighted by the submucosal glands and is free of carcinoma. B ESD specimen with early submucosal invasion in an adenocarcinoma involving the gastro-oesophageal junction (pT1b). The depth of submucosal invasion is measured from the deepest aspect of the second muscularis mucosae (double arrowhead). The deep margin of resection is negative. C ESD specimen; pT1b with positive deep margin. Low-grade adenocarcinoma with deep submucosal invasion extending to the deep margin of resection in this ESD specimen. However, the deep component is well circumscribed and appears to have been shelled out completely. D Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) specimen with a pT1b adenocarcinoma. D2-40 immunostain highlights a focus of lymphatic invasion (arrow), a high-risk feature for nodal metastasis.

A well-differentiated adenocarcinoma infiltrating through the muscularis mucosa. The cytological appearance of neoplastic glands is quite bland, but there is complete loss of normal crypt architecture. The irregular haphazard infiltrative glandular architecture is diagnostic of adenocarcinoma.

A Poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma with neoplastic cells present in small clusters, cords, and single cells. The associated low-grade, conventional, gland-forming adenocarcinoma component can be seen at the top of the image.
B Poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma with sheets of tumour cells showing marked nuclear atypia. Scattered foci of abortive gland formation with mucin are diagnostic of adenocarcinoma.
A Low-grade oesophageal adenocarcinoma with tubulopapillary architecture and increased intratumoural lymphocytes. MLH1/PMS2 showed complete loss of nuclear staining in the tumour cells.
B MLH1 loss in tubulopapillary adenocarcinoma. MLH1 immunostain shows complete loss of staining.
A Mucinous adenocarcinoma pattern with neoplastic glands, clusters, and single cells floating in pools of extracellular mucin.

D Oesophageal adenocarcinoma with enteroblastic differentiation. The architecture is tubulopapillary, and the neoplastic cells show clear cytoplasmic vacuoles mimicking the appearance of the fetal gut. The tumour cells were diffusely positive for SALL4 and focally for HepPar1; the serum AFP level was markedly elevated.

A ERBB2 (HER2) immunoscore 1+. HER2 immunostain is widely used as a biomarker in oesophagogastric adenocarcinomas. Intratumoural heterogeneity in HER2 expression is well recognized in these tumours. The primary tumour shown here was negative with only faint membranous staining (arrows) in rare tumour cells.
B The cervical lymph node metastasis from the same tumour was positive and showed diffuse strong membranous staining in > 75% of the tumour cells. ERBB2 (HER2) immunoscore 3+.
A Sheets of tumour cells displaying large nuclei with fine chromatin; small nucleoli; and pale, vacuolated cytoplasm.
B PDL1 immunostain (clone: E1L3N) with a high combined positive score (CPS). Strong membranous staining is present in both tumour cells and tumour-infiltrating mononuclear cells.
Claudin-18.2 is a biomarker used for guiding therapy in oesophageal adenocarcinoma. The example shown here shows moderate to strong membranous staining in > 95% of the tumour cells.

Patient with an adenocarcinoma of the distal oesophagus extending to the oesophagogastric junction. Histological type: tubulopapillary and mucinous, with signet-ring cell appearance. Histological grade: G3 (according to WHO 2025); TNM eighth edition: pT1b. A Axial fused 18F-FDG PET/CT at the level of the oesophageal tumour, showing intense tracer uptake (maximum standardized uptake value [SUVmax]: 9.2). B Contrast-enhanced CT at the level of the oesophageal tumour, showing a moderate enhancement. C Oesophagogastroduodenoscopy (OGD) demonstrates the tumour that developed in a segment of Barrett oesophagus as a vegetating lesion. D Oesophageal adenocarcinoma in Barrett oesophagus (original magnification: 10×) obtained by mucosectomy, with classic G1 foci on the left and poorly differentiated and mucinous areas on the right. Note that the tumour is close to deep surgical margins. E High magnification (original magnification: 100×) showing intestinal metaplasia of Barrett oesophagus transitioning to adenocarcinoma infiltrating the submucosa; residual squamous oesophageal mucosa is also evident. H&E.
